tagline: An engineered living dressing that breaks open wound biofilm, clears pathogens and supports tissue repair in chronic wounds
tagline_zh: 一種工程化活體敷料，能破壞傷口生物膜、清除病原菌，並支持慢性傷口的組織修復
summary: SJTU-BioX-Shanghai built Dual-Armor, an engineered-microbe dressing for chronic wounds, targeting the biofilm that a meta-analysis of 2,666 chronic wounds found in 68% of cases; about 18.6 million people develop diabetic foot ulcers each year and roughly 65% recur within five years. The team's inclusivity work is the most systematically theorised of the 2026 cohort: they built a two-layer framework in which four dimensions (VOICE, OPPORTUNITY, ACCESSIBILITY, PARTICIPATION) locate where participation is blocked and a five-step pathway, HEALS (Hear, Examine, Act, Learn, Share), governs how each barrier is answered. Twelve activities are each written up against both layers, and patient input visibly changed the product: Dual-Armor was repositioned from a stand-alone treatment to an auxiliary post-debridement dressing, and patients' fear of live bacteria touching the wound drove the physical-containment hardware design.
summary_zh: SJTU-BioX-Shanghai 做出 Dual-Armor，一款用於慢性傷口的工程菌敷料，針對的是生物膜——一項涵蓋 2,666 例慢性傷口的統合分析發現其中 68% 有生物膜；每年約有 1,860 萬人罹患糖尿病足潰瘍，約 65% 在五年內復發。該隊的包容性工作是 2026 年各隊中理論化最系統的：他們建立了一個雙層架構，以四個面向（VOICE、OPPORTUNITY、ACCESSIBILITY、PARTICIPATION）定位參與在哪裡受阻，並以五步路徑 HEALS（Hear、Examine、Act、Learn、Share）規範每一道障礙如何被回應。十二項活動都分別對照兩個層次寫成紀錄，病人的意見也明顯改變了產品：Dual-Armor 從獨立療法重新定位為清創後的輔助敷料，而病人對活菌接觸傷口的恐懼促成了實體圍阻硬體的設計。

dry.frameworks: Self-built two-layer inclusivity framework: four dimensions named by the question each asks - VOICE (Can I be heard?), OPPORTUNITY (Can I get in?), ACCESSIBILITY (Can I engage in a way that works for me?), PARTICIPATION (Can I stay and contribute?) - plus HEALS (Hear, Examine, Act, Learn, Share) as the common action pathway every activity follows. Education was mapped onto three learner pathways (students: Understand to Learn to Create; public: Encounter to Understand; peer educators: Share to Adapt to Continue) and grounded in Constructionism and UDL 3.0, applied retrospectively as a mirror rather than imposed in advance. Photovoice was used with a proper citation to Wang and Burris (1997).
dry.frameworks_zh: 自建的雙層包容性架構：四個面向各以它所提出的問題命名——VOICE（我能被聽見嗎？）、OPPORTUNITY（我能進得來嗎？）、ACCESSIBILITY（我能以適合自己的方式參與嗎？）、PARTICIPATION（我能留下來並有所貢獻嗎？）——再加上 HEALS（Hear、Examine、Act、Learn、Share），作為每一項活動共同遵循的行動路徑。教育工作對應到三條學習者路徑（學生：理解—學習—創造；大眾：接觸—理解；同儕教育者：分享—調整—延續），並以建構論與 UDL 3.0 為基礎，但是回溯性地當成一面檢視的鏡子，而非事前強加的框架。Photovoice 的使用也正確引用了 Wang 與 Burris（1997）。
dry.dataviz: Co-designed care journey maps with colour-coded burden stickers marking pain, inconvenience, cost and psychological pressure; a handbook development flow figure; the four-dimension and HEALS framework figures; stakeholder overview of included groups.
dry.dataviz_zh: 共同設計的照護歷程圖，以顏色標示的負擔貼紙標記疼痛、不便、費用與心理壓力；手冊開發流程圖；四面向與 HEALS 架構圖；納入族群的利害關係人總覽。
dry.datascience: Paired pre/post questionnaires across activities: six patient questionnaires and six in-depth inpatient interviews with published anonymised results (66.7% had three or more episodes of infection, worsening or recurrence in the previous year; 83.3% described the wound's impact on daily life as large or very large); the Beneath the Wound role-play playtest collected five anonymous questionnaires at a 100% response rate, with mean self-rated understanding of five core concepts rising from 1.8 to 3.52/5, understanding of MRSA from 1.2 to 3.4/5 (the largest gain), inclusivity-experience mean 4.03/5, and 'every role carried real weight' and 'the host favored no position' both 4.4/5; pre/post testing at the Life Science x AI summer camp. The team repeatedly states sample limits rather than overclaiming.
dry.datascience_zh: 各項活動都採配對的前後測問卷：六份病人問卷與六場住院病人深度訪談，並公開去識別化結果（66.7% 在過去一年內有三次以上的感染、惡化或復發；83.3% 形容傷口對日常生活的影響為大或非常大）；「Beneath the Wound」角色扮演試玩收回五份匿名問卷，回收率 100%，五項核心概念的自評理解度平均從 1.8 升到 3.52/5，對 MRSA 的理解從 1.2 升到 3.4/5（增幅最大），包容性體驗平均 4.03/5，「每個角色都有實際份量」與「主持人不偏袒任何立場」都是 4.4/5；Life Science x AI 夏令營也做了前後測。該隊一再說明樣本的限制，而不是過度宣稱。
dry.software: Two open-source tools, both built from a named barrier. LabSafeMom gives pregnant, pregnancy-planning or breastfeeding researchers per-protocol risk guidance: submit a protocol and get a structured risk overview, safety controls and a PPE checklist against a knowledge base of 119 hazard entries built from public occupational-health references including NIOSH. Critically it has two separated modes - Basic runs entirely in the browser against a local deterministic rule set with no generative model, so the same input always yields the same reasoning and every score is traceable to a stated rule and reference; Enhanced adds natural-language protocol analysis only when the user supplies their own API key, and risk scores still come from auditable rules. Every report states it is an aid for discussion with an institutional EHS office and a qualified clinician, never a substitute. LabMate reduces bench friction for new researchers: it ingests protocols as PDF, TXT, Markdown, CSV or pasted text in Chinese or English, generates a preparation checklist, guides steps with smart timers, keeps an exportable lab record (Markdown, text or print), offers a Chinese-English toggle, four themes (Light, Lab, Dark, Sunset) and large-font options, and runs locally and offline with privacy-first handling.
dry.software_zh: 兩項開源工具，都是從一項被指名的障礙出發做出來的。LabSafeMom 為懷孕、準備懷孕或哺乳中的研究人員提供逐一實驗流程的風險指引：送入一份流程，就得到結構化的風險總覽、安全管制措施與個人防護裝備檢核表，依據的是一個含 119 筆危害條目的知識庫，由 NIOSH 等公開職業衛生資料建立。關鍵在於它有兩個彼此分離的模式——Basic 完全在瀏覽器中依本地的確定性規則集運作，不用生成式模型，因此同樣的輸入永遠得到同樣的推論，每個分數都可追溯到明確的規則與出處；Enhanced 只在使用者自行提供 API key 時才加入自然語言的流程分析，而風險分數仍然來自可稽核的規則。每份報告都註明它是與校內 EHS 單位及合格臨床醫師討論時的輔助，絕不是替代。LabMate 則降低新進研究人員在實驗台上的摩擦：可讀入 PDF、TXT、Markdown、CSV 或直接貼上的中英文流程文字，生成準備檢核表，以智慧計時器引導步驟，保留可匯出的實驗紀錄（Markdown、純文字或列印），提供中英文切換、四種主題（Light、Lab、Dark、Sunset）與大字型選項，並以隱私優先的方式在本地離線運作。
stack: browser-based deterministic rule engine (LabSafeMom Basic mode)
accessible web front end with dyslexia-font and animation toggles
techniques: physical containment hardware for live-bacteria dressings

good.publicEngagement: The framing sentence is the one to steal: 'Open is not enough. A door can stand open while some people never have the chance to reach it.' Under VOICE, the team visited the vascular disease department of Shanghai Hospital of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine, collecting six patient questionnaires and six in-depth inpatient interviews plus conversations with attending clinicians and ward care workers, and published the bilingual instrument and the anonymised results as PDFs. Patients' top fears were recurrent infection, healing time, pain and amputation risk; clinicians focused on debridement, exudate management and dressing fit; care workers identified post-discharge dressing changes and disinfection as the weakest link in the care chain. This directly repositioned Dual-Armor as an auxiliary dressing for continuous post-debridement care and drove the physical-containment hardware. A Photovoice study then handed the camera to patients, who chose which objects and scenes represented their treatment - wheelchairs, bedside equipment, nursing supplies - and explained why; for inpatients who could not shoot themselves, the team operated the camera but the subject, the explanation and the consent to display always remained the participant's. The authorised, de-identified photographs with the participants' own accounts became an exhibition at Shanghai Jiao Tong University that drew more than one hundred visits, with faces, wound close-ups, bed numbers and records deliberately excluded. The team's reflection is unusually principled: 'creating an opportunity for expression does not give the researchers ownership of the images', and the quality of an exhibition can never take priority over informed consent. Co-design went further: patients, caregivers and care workers drew the whole chronic-wound care journey with colour-coded stickers for pain, inconvenience, cost and psychological pressure, and caregivers added the hidden labour of accompanying visits and watching for abnormalities. The questions they raised repeatedly ('what do I do when the dressing sticks to the wound?', 'which smell means something is wrong?') became the actual table of contents of a 23-page Home-Care Handbook, which translates professional guidance into red-amber-green warning signals, a six-step dressing-change method and hand-fillable care record tables, deliberately offers an executable alternative after every 'do not do this', and gives separate dressing-change options for urban and primary-care settings. The draft was reviewed by clinicians from burn and reconstructive surgery and from endocrinology, who corrected the iodine and hydrogen peroxide guidance, the timing of diabetic foot care and primary-care dressing substitutes. The handbook is published free in Chinese and English, with printable appendix tables so it works for people without digital devices. The team also wrote Beneath the Wound, a 46-page host-facilitated ethics role-play (plus 10 pages of character cards in five- and six-player sets) in which players take the parts of a 72-year-old diabetic-foot patient, family members, the attending physician and ethics roles, and reach a decision with no standard answer over about two and a half hours; information is deliberately distributed - the physician holds risk data, the ethics member remembers past failures, the family waits for authority, the patient carries fear - so players must persuade each other with incomplete information. The full script and cards are released for other teams. Under OPPORTUNITY, the team ran no-prerequisite synthetic biology lessons at a middle school in Bazhong, Sichuan and a small rural class in Hou'an Village, Taizhou, Zhejiang, chosen precisely because students there rarely meet frontier science, using physical role-play of the central dogma and a 'Building a Cell Factory' design task, requiring no specialised equipment, delivered partly by video lesson in Hou'an, and evaluated with pre- and post-questionnaires; students produced their own posters, plasmid maps and models. These were followed by guided SJTU wet-lab visits to supply the missing middle step between a school lesson and university research, and by sustained mentoring of VGA-Pinion, a first-time US high-school team, from emails and online meetings through to an in-person Shanghai lab visit, with advice on project narrative, model-parameter grounding and Human Practices structure, always framed as ideas rather than decisions made for them. Under ACCESSIBILITY, 'Touch Life, See Hope' was a braille chronic-wound postcard co-creation at SJTU in which participants from several majors learned the braille alphabet, writing board and stylus, then discovered that accessibility is redesign rather than transcription - a tactile reader cannot skim, so messages had to be shortened, care advice separated from decorative text, and card layout built around how a finger moves; the cards carry Dual-Armor characters so sighted and non-sighted readers recognise them, and an 11-page English Braille Postcard Co-Creation Toolkit was released so others can run the session. 'Light Deep in the Lilong' is a sixteen-page bilingual illustrated story about Grandma Li, a 76-year-old retired Chinese-language teacher with an unhealed diabetic foot wound, written for the readers conventional material ignores - above all children in the patient's family - with wound microbes as characters mapped one-to-one onto Dual-Armor's functional modules; a bilingual audio edition is in preparation so reading need not depend on sight, and the story was read live to students in Bazhong. The wiki itself is an accessibility artefact, prompted by a senior student with ADHD who reported reading difficulty on many websites: it uses the Okabe-Ito colourblind-safe palette (#E69F00, #56B4E9, #F0E442, #D55E00, #0072B2), a one-click dyslexia-friendly font toggle, a one-click animation kill switch and a reading progress bar. Under PARTICIPATION the team turned inward to people already in science, building LabSafeMom for pregnant researchers and LabMate for new bench members. Education also produced a Base-Pairing Challenge card game, a diabetes scripted game, 'Dual-Armor Werewolf' (a social-deduction game where E. coli, S. epidermidis, immune cells and S. aureus are the roles and naringenin mechanisms are built into role relationships), a picture book and audiobook, clay cell-model making, a bioethics debate with no preset answer, and a six-step student design task (Problem, Chassis, Function, Safety, Teamwork, Presentation). Finally, the team co-authored a cross-team Education Activity Handbook with other university iGEM teams, taking responsibility for Part 7 on spatialised education and exhibitions with their Urban Orienteering chapter, explicitly so that future iGEMers do not start from scratch.
good.publicEngagement_zh: 值得借用的是那句定調的話：「開放還不夠。門可以一直開著，但有些人始終沒有機會走到門前。」在 VOICE 面向，該隊走訪上海市中西醫結合醫院的周圍血管科，收集六份病人問卷與六場住院病人深度訪談，並與主治醫師及病房照護員對談，再把雙語問卷工具與去識別化結果以 PDF 公開。病人最害怕的是感染復發、癒合時間、疼痛與截肢風險；臨床醫師關注清創、滲液管理與敷料貼合度；照護員指出出院後的換藥與消毒是整條照護鏈最弱的一環。這直接把 Dual-Armor 重新定位為清創後持續照護用的輔助敷料，也推動了實體圍阻硬體。接著的 Photovoice 研究把相機交給病人，由他們自己選擇哪些物件與場景代表自己的治療——輪椅、床邊設備、護理用品——並說明原因；對無法自己拍攝的住院病人，由團隊代為操作相機，但拍攝對象、說明內容與展示的同意權始終屬於參與者。這些經授權、去識別化的照片連同參與者自己的敘述，成為上海交通大學的一場展覽，參觀超過一百人次，並刻意排除臉部、傷口特寫、床號與病歷。該隊的反思格外有原則：「創造一個表達的機會，並不等於研究者取得了影像的所有權」，展覽的品質也絕不能優先於知情同意。共同設計走得更遠：病人、家屬照顧者與照護員一起畫出完整的慢性傷口照護歷程，用不同顏色的貼紙標記疼痛、不便、費用與心理壓力，照顧者還補上了陪同就醫與留意異常這些看不見的勞動。他們反覆提出的問題（「敷料黏在傷口上的時候該怎麼辦？」、「哪一種氣味代表出了問題？」）直接成為一本 23 頁《居家照護手冊》的實際目錄。手冊把專業指引轉譯成紅—黃—綠三級警示訊號、六步換藥法與可手寫填寫的照護紀錄表，刻意在每一句「不要這樣做」之後都給出一個可執行的替代做法，並針對都市與基層醫療場域分別提供換藥選項。草稿由燒傷整形外科與新陳代謝科的臨床醫師審閱，他們修正了碘與過氧化氫的使用指引、糖尿病足照護的時機，以及基層可用的敷料替代品。手冊以中英文免費公開，並附可列印的附錄表格，讓沒有數位裝置的人也用得上。該隊還寫了《Beneath the Wound》，一份 46 頁、由主持人帶領的倫理角色扮演腳本（另有 10 頁角色卡，分五人與六人兩種配置），玩家分別扮演一位 72 歲的糖尿病足病人、家屬、主治醫師與倫理相關角色，在約兩個半小時內做出一個沒有標準答案的決定；資訊被刻意分散配置——醫師掌握風險數據、倫理成員記得過去的失敗、家屬等待權威表態、病人承受恐懼——因此玩家必須在資訊不完整的情況下彼此說服。完整腳本與角色卡已釋出給其他隊伍。在 OPPORTUNITY 面向，該隊在四川巴中的一所國中與浙江台州后安村的一個小型鄉村班級開設零先修要求的合成生物學課程，選這兩個地點正是因為當地學生少有機會接觸前沿科學；課程用肢體角色扮演演示中心法則，加上一項「打造細胞工廠」的設計任務，完全不需要專門器材，在后安村有一部分以影片授課，並以前後測問卷評估；學生自己做出海報、質體圖譜與模型。之後再安排到上海交大的導覽式濕實驗室參訪，補上學校課程與大學研究之間缺掉的中間一環；另外也長期輔導首次參賽的美國高中隊伍 VGA-Pinion，從電子郵件、線上會議一路到實地到上海參訪實驗室，在專案敘事、模型參數依據與 Human Practices 架構上提供建議，而且一貫定位為提供想法，不是替他們做決定。在 ACCESSIBILITY 面向，「Touch Life, See Hope」是在上海交大舉辦的點字慢性傷口明信片共創活動，來自多個系所的參與者先學點字字母、點字板與點字筆，接著就發現無障礙是重新設計而不是逐字轉譯——觸覺讀者無法快速瀏覽，所以訊息必須縮短、照護建議必須與裝飾性文字分開，卡片版面也要照手指移動的方式重新安排；卡片上放了 Dual-Armor 的角色，讓視覺與非視覺讀者都認得出來，並釋出一份 11 頁的英文點字明信片共創工具包，讓別人也能照著辦。「Light Deep in the Lilong」是一則 16 頁的雙語繪本故事，主角是李奶奶，一位 76 歲、退休的國文老師，有一處遲遲未癒的糖尿病足傷口；故事寫給傳統素材忽略的讀者，尤其是病人家裡的孩子，傷口微生物被寫成角色，並與 Dual-Armor 的功能模組一一對應；雙語有聲版正在製作，讓閱讀不必依賴視覺，故事也在巴中現場朗讀給學生聽。wiki 本身就是一件無障礙產出，起因是一位患有 ADHD 的高年級學生反映許多網站讀起來很吃力：網站採用 Okabe-Ito 色盲友善配色（#E69F00、#56B4E9、#F0E442、#D55E00、#0072B2）、一鍵切換的讀寫障礙友善字型、一鍵關閉動畫，以及閱讀進度條。在 PARTICIPATION 面向，該隊轉向已經身在科學領域裡的人，為懷孕的研究人員做 LabSafeMom，為新進實驗室成員做 LabMate。教育方面也產出了鹼基配對挑戰卡牌遊戲、糖尿病劇本遊戲、「Dual-Armor 狼人殺」（一款社交推理遊戲，角色就是 E. coli、S. epidermidis、免疫細胞與 S. aureus，柚皮素的作用機制則寫進了角色關係裡）、一本繪本與有聲書、黏土細胞模型製作、一場沒有預設答案的生物倫理辯論，以及一項六步驟的學生設計任務（問題、載體、功能、安全、團隊合作、簡報）。最後，該隊與其他大學 iGEM 隊伍合著了一本跨隊《教育活動手冊》，負責第 7 章空間化教育與展覽的部分，貢獻「城市定向」一章，明確就是為了讓未來的 iGEMer 不必從零開始。
good.ihp: The project began with a team member's own fall injury and the experience of caring for the wound. Patient and caregiver evidence was treated as design input rather than validation: ward findings are documented on the Integrated Human Practices page and traced through to three specific changes (product repositioning to post-debridement auxiliary dressing, physical containment of live bacteria, and the decision to co-write a care handbook with clinical staff). The team draws an explicit principle: patients may not decide gene circuits or material parameters, but they decide what the technology must respond to, and lack of specialist knowledge is never a reason to exclude them from design. Limits are stated rather than hidden - six patients cannot represent everyone, and acceptance expressed in a hypothetical interview must still be verified in real use.
good.ihp_zh: 專案的起點是一位隊員自己跌倒受傷、並照護那處傷口的經驗。病人與照顧者的證據被當成設計輸入，而不是事後驗證：病房訪查的發現記錄在 Integrated Human Practices 頁面，並一路追溯到三項具體改變（產品重新定位為清創後輔助敷料、活菌的實體圍阻，以及決定與臨床人員共同撰寫照護手冊）。該隊明確提出一項原則：病人也許不決定基因迴路或材料參數，但他們決定這項技術必須回應什麼，而缺乏專業知識永遠不能成為把他們排除在設計之外的理由。限制是寫明的而非藏起來的——六位病人無法代表所有人，在假設性訪談中表達的接受度，仍然必須在真實使用中驗證。
good.realWorld: Open, reusable outputs: the 23-page Home-Care Handbook in Chinese and English with printable records; the Beneath the Wound full script, host guide and character cards; the Braille Postcard Co-Creation Toolkit; the bilingual illustrated story and forthcoming audio edition; LabSafeMom and LabMate as live apps with open source; teaching decks for the central dogma, cell factory, bioethics debate and engineered-microorganism design; game cards; and the co-authored cross-team Education Activity Handbook. A beginner's guide for new iGEM teams covering schedule planning, stage tasks and common questions is planned for open release on the wiki.
good.realWorld_zh: 開放、可重複使用的產出：23 頁中英文《居家照護手冊》，附可列印的紀錄表；《Beneath the Wound》的完整腳本、主持人指南與角色卡；點字明信片共創工具包；雙語繪本故事與即將推出的有聲版；LabSafeMom 與 LabMate 都是可直接使用的應用程式並且開源；中心法則、細胞工廠、生物倫理辯論與工程微生物設計的教學簡報；遊戲卡牌；以及合著的跨隊《教育活動手冊》。另有一份給 iGEM 新隊伍的入門指南，涵蓋時程規劃、各階段任務與常見問題，計畫在 wiki 上公開釋出。

gemsTakeaway: Adopt SJTU's two-layer discipline: classify every engagement by which barrier it removes (can I be heard, get in, engage in my format, stay and contribute) and run each one through Hear-Examine-Act-Learn-Share, ending every activity with a downloadable artefact someone else can run - a toolkit, a script, a handbook - and a written statement of what the evidence does not prove.
gemsTakeaway_zh: 值得借用 SJTU 的雙層紀律：把每一項參與活動依它所排除的障礙分類（我能被聽見嗎、我能進得來嗎、我能用適合自己的形式參與嗎、我能留下來並有所貢獻嗎），並讓每一項都走完 Hear-Examine-Act-Learn-Share，每項活動都以一份別人可以直接拿去執行的可下載產出作結——工具包、腳本、手冊——再加上一段明白寫出證據尚未能證明什麼的說明。
